title: The Salt Road
author: Imogen Wray
description: A caravan trader crosses a dying empire to deliver a letter that could end a war, discovering along the way that the desert keeps better records than any archive.

title: Learning React Deeply
author: Marcus Odell
description: A practical, no-fluff walkthrough of component architecture, hooks, and rendering performance for developers who want to actually understand the framework, not just use it.

title: The Quiet Universe
author: Dr. Amara Solis
description: An accessible tour of cosmology's biggest open questions, from dark matter to the fate of the last star, written for curious readers with no physics background.

title: Paper Lanterns
author: Hana Ito
description: Three generations of a family run a lantern shop through a century of change, and each lantern they sell carries a wish someone was too afraid to say aloud.

title: Systems That Don't Fall Over
author: Priya Nathan
description: Case studies and design patterns for building distributed systems that survive real-world failure, drawn from a decade of on-call incidents at scale.

title: The Chemistry of Everyday Things
author: Owen Farrow
description: Why bread rises, why rust forms, why coffee tastes different at altitude — a tour of the ordinary chemical reactions hiding in daily life.

title: A Cartography of Small Griefs
author: Noor Abbasi
description: A poet maps the geography of loss across a single year, charting how grief moves through a house, a city, and eventually, a person.

title: Databases Without Fear
author: Julius Kwan
description: A friendly, example-driven guide to relational and document databases, covering schema design, indexing, and the trade-offs that actually matter in production.

title: The Migration
author: Dr. Femi Okoro
description: A field biologist's account of following one bird species across four continents, and what its shrinking migration route reveals about a changing planet.

title: Nine Doors to Kestrel House
author: Rosalind Vane
description: A locked-room mystery set in a crumbling estate where every door in the house has a secret, and only one leads to the truth about the owner's disappearance.

title: Designing APIs People Actually Like
author: Sana Malik
description: A practical handbook on API ergonomics — naming, versioning, error design, and documentation — for teams that want fewer support tickets and happier integrators.

title: The Mathematics of Tides
author: Dr. Liam Bergström
description: An elegant explanation of the gravitational dance between moon, sun, and ocean, and how coastal communities have read the tides for a thousand years.
